title: pKa ladder
note: Lecture values are what this exam expects. Where the usual tables differ, the literature value is given.

rows.name: hydroiodic acid
rows.why: Huge atom: the charge of iodide is spread over a large volume (size).

rows.name: hydrobromic acid
rows.why: Large atom: size.

rows.name: hydrochloric acid
rows.why: Size and electronegativity.

rows.name: p-toluenesulfonic acid
rows.why: The charge of tosylate is shared by three oxygens (resonance): an excellent leaving group.

rows.name: hydronium
rows.why: A positively charged acid: losing the proton gives neutral water.

rows.name: trifluoroacetic acid
rows.why: Resonance, plus three fluorines pulling electron density through the bonds (induction).

rows.name: hydrofluoric acid
rows.why: Fluoride is small: the charge is concentrated, so it is the strongest base of the halides and a poor leaving group.

rows.name: carboxylic acid (acetic acid)
rows.why: The charge of the carboxylate is shared by two oxygens (resonance).

rows.name: hydrogen sulfide
rows.why: Sulfur is larger than oxygen and spreads out the charge (size): more acidic than water.

rows.name: phenol
rows.why: The charge of phenoxide is delocalized into the ring (resonance).

rows.name: ammonium ion
rows.why: A positively charged acid: losing the proton gives the neutral amine.

rows.name: thiol
rows.why: Like hydrogen sulfide: the large sulfur stabilizes the charge.

rows.name: methanol
rows.why: The small methoxide ion is well solvated: the most acidic simple alcohol in solution.

rows.name: water
rows.why: Oxygen is electronegative, but the charge of hydroxide sits on one small atom.

rows.name: ethanol
rows.why: An ordinary alcohol: about 16.

rows.name: isopropanol
rows.why: A bulkier alkoxide is less well solvated, so the alcohol is a little less acidic.

rows.name: tert-butanol
rows.why: The bulkiest alkoxide is the least solvated: the least acidic in solution (in the gas phase the order reverses).

rows.name: terminal alkyne (acetylene, propyne)
rows.why: The lone pair of the anion is in an sp orbital, 50% s character, held close to the nucleus (hybridization).

rows.name: amine or ammonia N-H
rows.why: Nitrogen is less electronegative than oxygen, so its anion is less stable.

rows.name: alkane C-H
rows.why: An sp3 carbanion has nothing to stabilize it: the strongest bases. Lecture: 50 to 60.
